content.title: About
content.content: Canned asparagus cooked in vegetable oil consists of selected asparagus spears that are peeled, blanched and packed in glass or metal jars with added oil. The product is ready to eat and retains the characteristic aroma, a pleasant bite and the nutritional qualities of fresh asparagus.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus has been cultivated for more than 2,000 years, dating back to ancient Egypt and Rome.
Canning extends the shelf life to 2–3 years while preserving flavor and nutrients.
The oil (often olive or sunflower) enhances taste and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
Heat treatment increases the concentration of aromatic compounds that give asparagus its distinctive scent.
In many countries canned asparagus is a popular ingredient in salads, appetizers and as a side dish for meat.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate (vitamin B9) supports cell division and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Asparagus provides glutathione, vitamin C and carotenoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup of canned asparagus (≈150 g) contains about 30 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly food.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Allergy to amaranth family vegetables
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to asparagus.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should account for it.

items.title: Oil content
items.content: The added oil increases the caloric density; portion control is advisable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Bacterial safety
items.content: Damaged cans (dents, bulging) may compromise safety and should be discarded.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned asparagus can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, pastas, omelets, or used in hot dishes such as stews and casseroles. It is often briefly warmed in a skillet with a little extra oil before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct light. After opening, transfer the asparagus to an airtight container and keep it refrigerated for 3–4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
